fact.claim: The S&P/TSX Composite fell 37% from February 19 to March 23, 2020, and closed at a low of 11,228. On November 4, 2026 it stood at 36,341.40, so $10,000 that followed the index from the low would be worth about $32,400 today. That figure counts price changes only. A real index fund would also have paid dividends, minus its fees, and selling at the bottom locked in the loss. Past returns are not a promise of future returns.

plain.what: In March 2020, Canada's stock market fell fast. The TSX is a list of Canada's biggest companies, tracked all together as one number. It dropped 37% in 33 days, from February 19 to March 23, 2020, and closed at a low of 11,228 on the worst day.
plain.so_what: $10,000 that followed that list from the low would be about $32,400 today, counting price only, while money that was sold at the bottom stayed at $6,300.
plain.do: Open your bank or investing app today and write down the name of the fund you hold and how many companies are inside it.
